Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the TechGlobal Solutions Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Kim, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Kim, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to TechGlobal Solutions’ Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Anya Sharma, CEO; David Chen, CFO; and Marcus Lee, EVP of Operations and Innovation.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Dr. Sharma.

Dr. Anya Sharma, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. We anticipate a challenging operating environment in the third quarter of 2020. While the memory market continues to demonstrate resilience, the escalating impact of the COVID-19 pandemic will exert downward pressure on demand across several key product segments, leading to an anticipated sequential decline in overall revenue and a contraction in gross margin. We project Q3 2020 revenue to be in the range of $1.95 billion to $2.05 billion. This represents a decrease of approximately 8% to 12% compared to the $2.23 billion reported in Q2 2020. While this represents a contraction quarter-over-quarter, it's important to note that this remains a 10% - 15% increase compared to Q3 2019 revenue of $1.78 billion. This year-over-year growth is primarily driven by the continued strength of our memory division, particularly in the server and mobile sectors, that experienced significant growth earlier in the year. We expect the memory division (DRAM and NAND flash) to contribute approximately 60-65% of total revenue in Q3 2020. We anticipate continued robust demand from data centers as cloud service providers continue to invest heavily in infrastructure to support remote work and increased online activity. Specifically, we project a 3% sequential increase in server DRAM revenue. Mobile DRAM demand is expected to remain stable, with modest growth driven by the introduction of new 5G-enabled smartphones, but offset by overall reduced consumer spending. However, pricing pressures are expected to intensify in NAND flash due to increased supply and competitive dynamics, which will negatively impact overall memory gross margins. The Logic and Microcontroller Division is expected to experience the most significant impact from COVID-19. We anticipate a 15% to 20% sequential decline in revenue due to disruptions in the automotive and industrial sectors. Automotive production has been severely curtailed in many regions, particularly in Europe and North America, leading to reduced demand for our automotive-grade microcontrollers. Similarly, the industrial sector is facing reduced capital expenditures and project delays, impacting demand for our industrial automation solutions. We are actively working with our customers to manage inventory levels and reschedule deliveries. Revenue from other product lines, including specialized sensors and embedded systems, is expected to decline by approximately 5% to 10% sequentially. This decline is primarily attributed to disruptions in the supply chain and reduced demand from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that are facing significant financial challenges. We anticipate Q3 2020 gross margin to be in the range of 38% to 40%. This represents a decrease of approximately 200 to 400 basis points compared to the 42% reported in Q2 2020. This contraction is primarily driven by lower revenue volume, which will negatively impact gross margin due to lower absorption of fixed costs. A shift in product mix towards memory, which typically has lower gross margins than logic and microcontrollers, will also contribute to the margin decline. While memory revenue is growing, the increased competition in the NAND market pressures gross margins in that specific area. Increased pricing pressure in the NAND flash market, coupled with promotional activities to stimulate demand in certain segments, will further erode gross margins. We are incurring additional costs related to employee safety measures, supply chain diversification, and logistics, which are negatively impacting gross margin. We expect to see moderate revenue declines in North America due to the impact of COVID-19 on the automotive and industrial sectors. However, demand from data centers is expected to remain strong. Europe is expected to be the most impacted region due to the severe disruptions in the automotive industry and the overall economic slowdown. We expect to see relatively stable revenue in Asia-Pacific, with continued growth in China driven by increased demand for 5G-enabled smartphones and cloud infrastructure. However, we are closely monitoring the situation in India and Southeast Asia, where the pandemic is still spreading rapidly. Despite the challenging environment, we remain focused on executing our strategic priorities. We are continuing to invest in new product development, including next-generation memory technologies, advanced microcontrollers, and innovative sensor solutions. We plan to launch several new products in the second half of 2020 that will address emerging market opportunities. We are implementing a range of cost optimization measures to mitigate the impact of lower revenue volume and increased pricing pressure. These measures include streamlining our operations, reducing discretionary spending, and improving supply chain efficiency. We are actively engaging with our customers to understand their evolving needs and provide them with customized solutions. We are also working to strengthen our partnerships with key distributors and system integrators. We are diversifying our supply chain to reduce our reliance on single sources and mitigate the risk of disruptions. We are also investing in advanced manufacturing technologies to improve our production efficiency and flexibility. While the near-term outlook is uncertain due to the evolving nature of the COVID-19 pandemic, we remain confident in our long-term growth prospects. We believe that our diversified product portfolio, strong customer relationships, and commitment to innovation will enable us to navigate these challenges and emerge stronger. We are closely monitoring the situation and will provide updates on our progress in future earnings calls. We anticipate a recovery in demand in the fourth quarter of 2020, but the timing and pace of the recovery will depend on the trajectory of the pandemic and the effectiveness of government stimulus measures. We are preparing for a wide range of potential scenarios and are committed to managing our business prudently and responsibly.

We also saw great momentum in the total consolidated revenue for Q1 2024, which reached KRW 55.3 trillion, representing a 7.6% decrease compared to the KRW 59.8 trillion recorded in Q4 2023. However, on a year-over-year basis, revenue saw a positive growth of 5.6% compared to KRW 52.4 trillion in Q1 2023. The sequential decline reflects the anticipated seasonal weakness in our Display Panel and Consumer Electronics (CE) divisions, exacerbated by persistent, albeit lessening, disruptions related to the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing global supply chain constraints. The YoY growth was primarily driven by strong demand in the memory semiconductor market and increased component sales linked to robust mobile device production from key customers. While the revenue fell short of our Q4 2023 guidance of KRW 57 trillion, the core drivers of growth remain robust, and we anticipate a stronger performance in the subsequent quarters. The 7.6% decrease in revenue from Q4 2023 to Q1 2024 can be attributed to a significant decline in our Display Panel division, with revenue falling by 15% from KRW 14.5 trillion in Q4 2023 to KRW 12.3 trillion in Q1 2024. This was primarily due to seasonality, as Q4 traditionally sees a surge in demand for premium OLED panels for TVs and high-end smartphones due to the holiday season, while Q1 is a traditionally weaker period. Increased competition from Chinese panel manufacturers in the LCD segment put downward pressure on average selling prices (ASPs). We saw a 5% decrease in LCD ASPs compared to Q4 2023. A shift towards smaller-sized panels for mobile devices, which have lower revenue per unit compared to larger TV panels, also contributed to the revenue decrease. The CE division, encompassing TVs, appliances, and audio products, experienced a 10% decrease in revenue from KRW 16 trillion in Q4 2023 to KRW 14.4 trillion in Q1 2024, again, due to seasonal weakness. Ongoing component shortages, particularly for microcontrollers and display drivers, continued to impact production volumes and lead times, hindering our ability to fully meet demand. Specifically, our premium TV production was down by approximately 8% due to these constraints. Rising inflation rates in key markets like North America and Europe impacted consumer spending on discretionary items, leading to a decrease in overall demand for our CE products. While the direct impact of COVID-19 has lessened compared to previous quarters, it still had a noticeable effect. Lockdowns in certain regions of China, particularly in manufacturing hubs, disrupted our supply chain and delayed shipments. We estimate that COVID-19 related disruptions negatively impacted our total revenue by approximately 2%. This was primarily due to lockdowns in the supply chains of the CE division. The 5.6% increase in revenue from KRW 52.4 trillion in Q1 2023 to KRW 55.3 trillion in Q1 2024 was primarily driven by strong growth in the Memory Semiconductor division, with revenue increasing by 18% YoY. This was fueled by continued expansion of data centers by cloud service providers and enterprise customers, which drove demand for high-capacity DRAM and NAND flash memory. We saw a particularly strong demand for our DDR5 modules, with sales increasing by over 300% YoY. Increased memory content in smartphones, particularly in high-end models, contributed to higher demand for our mobile DRAM and NAND solutions. The average memory capacity per smartphone increased by approximately 15% YoY. Favorable market conditions and tight supply led to an increase in ASPs for both DRAM and NAND flash memory. DRAM ASPs increased by approximately 10% YoY, while NAND ASPs increased by approximately 5% YoY. Increased sales of components, including application processors and camera modules, to mobile device manufacturers contributed to the YoY growth, driven by successful design wins in key smartphone models from leading manufacturers. Our advanced manufacturing capabilities, particularly in camera module technology, allowed us to capture a larger share of the market. While the Display Panel and CE divisions experienced QoQ declines, they showed slight YoY improvements compared to a weaker Q1 2023, partially due to improved supply chain conditions and a rebound in consumer demand in certain regions. Our Q1 2024 revenue of KRW 55.3 trillion fell short of our Q4 2023 guidance of KRW 57 trillion by approximately 3%. This variance was primarily due to weaker-than-expected display panel performance, persistent supply chain disruptions, and conservative guidance for memory.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to David to walk through in more detail.

David Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Anya, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Anya said, we are aware that while the overall market bit growth is projected to be in the low to mid-single digits for Q3 2024, we anticipate our bit growth to be slightly below the market average. This is primarily due to planned strategic shifts in our product mix towards higher-margin, value-added solutions within the Enterprise Storage and Mobile segments, which may temporarily impact overall bit shipment volumes. We remain confident in our ability to capture market share in key strategic areas and drive sustainable, profitable growth in the long term. Within Enterprise Storage, we anticipate a 3% sequential decrease in bit shipments for Q3 2024 compared to Q2 2024. This is attributable to a combination of factors, including a temporary pause in inventory build-up by a major hyperscale customer and a gradual transition towards our newer, higher-density NAND solutions, which require a longer qualification cycle with Enterprise clients. However, we project a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion within the Enterprise Storage segment, driven by higher average selling prices (ASPs) from the increased adoption of our high-capacity NVMe SSDs based on our 232-layer NAND technology. We are actively engaged with key customers on early testing and validation of our next-generation storage solutions, which we expect to contribute significantly to revenue growth in late Q4 2024 and into 2025. In Client SSDs, we forecast a flat bit shipment growth compared to Q2 2024. We believe this is indicative of a stabilization in the PC market after several quarters of inventory correction. We expect a 6% decrease in revenue year-over-year to $1.1 billion for the Client SSD segment. This is primarily due to continued pricing pressure in the entry-level PC market, despite the increasing adoption of SSDs over traditional hard disk drives. To counteract this, we are focusing on securing design wins with premium PC manufacturers for our high-performance PCIe Gen4 and Gen5 SSDs and investing in cost optimization initiatives to improve our competitiveness in the value segment. In the Mobile segment, we anticipate a 2% sequential increase in bit shipments for Q3 2024, driven by seasonal demand for new smartphone launches in the second half of the year, particularly in emerging markets like India and Southeast Asia. We forecast a 4% increase in revenue year-over-year to $800 million for the Mobile segment. Our strategy here involves offering a diversified portfolio of eMMC and UFS solutions to cater to different price points and performance requirements. We are also closely monitoring the developments in the foldable smartphone market, which presents a significant opportunity for high-density, high-performance storage solutions. The Consumer segment is facing headwinds due to declining demand for traditional removable storage devices. We forecast a 5% sequential decrease in bit shipments and a 10% decrease in revenue year-over-year to $300 million for the Consumer segment. Our strategy here is to focus on higher-margin products, such as high-capacity SD cards for professional photography and videography, and to explore new application areas for flash memory in the consumer electronics space. The successful ramp of our 232-layer NAND technology is critical to our long-term competitiveness. We are on track to achieve volume production of 232-layer NAND by the end of Q3 2024, which will enable us to offer higher-density, lower-cost storage solutions across all segments. We are investing heavily in developing advanced controller technology to optimize the performance and endurance of our SSDs. Our proprietary controller architecture allows us to differentiate our products and deliver superior customer value. We are actively expanding our presence in emerging markets to reduce our reliance on mature markets and forging strategic partnerships with key players in the ecosystem to accelerate the adoption of our storage solutions. This includes collaborations with cloud service providers, PC manufacturers, and mobile device makers. While it's premature to provide precise full-year guidance, our current projections indicate that our bit growth for FY2024 will likely be in the low single digits, slightly below the overall market growth. We expect revenue growth to be higher than bit growth, driven by higher ASPs and a favorable product mix. We remain committed to executing our strategic priorities and delivering sustainable, profitable growth for our shareholders.

We invested strategically in this area, resulting in our Q2 2024 operating margin standing at 18.2%, representing a notable shift from both the previous quarter (Q1 2024) and the same quarter last year (Q2 2023). Operating profit decreased by KRW 0.7 trillion QoQ, landing at KRW 6.4 trillion, translating to roughly a 9.8% decline from Q1 2024's KRW 7.1 trillion. The corresponding operating margin decreased from 20.1% in Q1 2024 to 18.2% in Q2 2024. This 1.9 percentage point decrease is primarily attributable to seasonal weakness in consumer electronics, which particularly impacted our display panel business, where demand for large-sized LCD panels decreased by approximately 12% QoQ, leading to a decrease in average selling prices (ASPs) of approximately 5%. This was further exacerbated by increased competition from Chinese manufacturers in the lower-end LCD segment, putting pressure on our margins. We strategically increased marketing spend by KRW 0.3 trillion in Q2 to support the launch of our new Galaxy S24 series and to promote our latest line of QLED TVs. While these launches were successful in terms of unit sales, the increased marketing expenditure inevitably impacted our operating margin in the short term. We anticipate seeing a stronger return on these investments in the second half of the year. The strengthening of the Korean Won against the US Dollar and the Euro had a negative impact on our export revenue. We estimate that currency fluctuations reduced our operating profit by approximately KRW 0.15 trillion in Q2. While overall operating profit declined, it's crucial to note that our memory division performed exceptionally well. Increased demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI applications, coupled with tight supply conditions, led to a 15% increase in Q2 revenue year-over-year to KRW 10.2 trillion in this segment, and a significant improvement in memory operating margins. This partially offset the negative impact from other business segments. Despite the quarterly headwinds, we continued to invest heavily in R&D related to next-generation technologies such as 3nm process technology and advanced packaging solutions for AI chips. While these investments did not contribute to immediate revenue generation, they are critical for maintaining our competitive edge in the long run. Compared to Q2 2023, operating profit increased by KRW 0.2 trillion, and the operating margin improved from 17.5% in Q2 2023 to 18.2% in Q2 2024, reflecting the strategic initiatives that have taken place over the past year. This is a positive sign indicating the company's overall health. Our mobile business achieved a significant improvement in product mix, with a higher proportion of sales coming from premium devices like the Galaxy S24 Ultra and the Z Fold 5. This shift towards higher-margin products contributed significantly to the YoY increase in operating profit. The ASP for our mobile phones increased by approximately 8% YoY. We successfully diversified our customer base for mobile OLED displays, securing new contracts with several major Chinese smartphone manufacturers. This reduced our reliance on a single customer and improved our bargaining power, leading to better pricing and higher margins. Our mobile OLED revenue from Chinese customers increased by approximately 20% YoY. We implemented a company-wide cost optimization program in late 2023, targeting improvements in manufacturing efficiency, supply chain management, and administrative overhead. These initiatives have started to yield tangible results, contributing to a reduction in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue. We estimate that cost optimization contributed approximately KRW 0.1 trillion to the YoY improvement in operating profit. In our Q1 2024 earnings call, we provided guidance for a Q2 2024 operating margin in the range of 19.0% to 20.0%. Our actual operating margin of 18.2% fell short of this guidance by approximately 0.8 to 1.8 percentage points due to a stronger-than-expected consumer electronics slowdown, increased competition in LCD panels, and the impact of geopolitical factors. Despite the Q2 challenges, we remain optimistic about the long-term prospects for our business. We are confident that our investments in R&D, coupled with our strategic focus on high-growth areas like AI and 5G, will drive future revenue and profit growth. We are taking the following actions to address the challenges and improve our performance in the second half of the year, including aggressively managing costs, focusing on value-added products and services, strengthening our partnerships, monitoring macroeconomic factors, and optimizing marketing spends. We expect to see an improvement in our operating margin in the second half of the year as seasonal demand recovers and the benefits of our strategic initiatives materialize. We will continue to closely monitor the market environment and make adjustments to our strategy as needed to ensure we deliver sustainable value to our shareholders.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in our gross margin. TechGlobal Solutions reported a gross profit of KRW20.5 trillion in Q3 2024, a decrease of KRW0.8 trillion compared to Q2 2024. Despite this decline in absolute gross profit, our gross margin improved slightly to 37.1%, exceeding our guidance of 36.5% set during the Q2 earnings call. This reflects successful cost optimization initiatives and a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin offerings, partially offsetting revenue headwinds in specific regional markets. We remain cautiously optimistic about maintaining this positive margin trend in Q4, despite anticipated seasonal pressures. Gross profit decreased by KRW0.8 trillion, falling from KRW21.3 trillion in Q2 2024 to KRW20.5 trillion in Q3 2024, representing a 3.8% decrease. Despite the lower gross profit, the gross margin increased slightly from 36.8% in Q2 2024 to 37.1% in Q3 2024. This 0.3 percentage point improvement is primarily attributable to our ongoing "Project Phoenix" initiative, focused on streamlining supply chain operations and negotiating more favorable component pricing, which yielded tangible results in Q3. Specifically, we achieved a 5% reduction in the cost of goods sold (COGS) for our flagship smartphone line, the "Galaxy X Series," which directly contributed to the improved margin. We expect further gains from this initiative in Q4. We witnessed a strong uptake in sales of our high-margin enterprise software solutions and premium cloud services. Revenue from these segments grew by 12% QoQ, driven by increased adoption among large corporations undergoing digital transformation. This shift towards higher-margin products helped offset the impact of lower sales volume in some of our lower-margin consumer electronics segments. Year-over-year, gross profit increased by KRW1.2 trillion from KRW19.3 trillion in Q3 2023 to KRW20.5 trillion in Q3 2024, representing a 6.2% increase. The gross margin improved significantly year-over-year, rising from 35.5% in Q3 2023 to 37.1% in Q3 2024, a 1.6 percentage point improvement. In Q4 2023 and Q1 2024, we implemented strategic price increases across select product lines, particularly in regions with robust demand and limited competitive pressure. This contributed significantly to the YoY margin improvement. Investment in advanced manufacturing technologies, such as automation and AI-powered quality control, at our production facilities in Vietnam and India, resulted in a 7% reduction in manufacturing defects and a 3% improvement in production efficiency. These gains translated directly into lower COGS and higher gross margins. We saw increased customer adoption of our extended warranty, repair and maintenance, and software subscription services. This part of our business now accounts for a larger portion of our revenue and is typically higher margin than product sales. During the Q2 2024 earnings call, we guided for a gross margin of 36.5% for Q3 2024. Our actual gross margin of 37.1% exceeded this guidance by 0.6 percentage points due to stronger-than-anticipated enterprise sales, favorable currency exchange rates, and the delayed impact of component price increases. Gross margin in North America increased by 1.2 percentage points YoY, driven by strong demand for our premium smartphones and enterprise software. Europe saw a slight decline in gross margin (0.3 percentage points YoY) due to increased competition and promotional activity in the consumer electronics market. The Asia-Pacific region experienced a significant improvement in gross margin (2.0 percentage points YoY) due to the successful launch of new mid-range smartphones and the growing adoption of our cloud services in emerging markets. While we are pleased with the Q3 gross margin performance, we remain focused on continuous improvement. We are actively exploring opportunities to further optimize our supply chain, enhance our product mix, and expand our service offerings. We are also closely monitoring global economic conditions and geopolitical risks, which could potentially impact our future performance. Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we anticipate seasonal pressures and increased marketing expenses related to the holiday season. However, we are confident that our ongoing cost optimization initiatives and product mix diversification will enable us to maintain a healthy gross margin, targeting a range of 36.8% - 37.3%.

Now I’ll turn it over to Marcus, who will speak about operations and innovation.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in gross margin. Can you talk more about the regional performance and the drivers behind the outperformance in Asia-Pacific?

David Chen:
Certainly. As we highlighted, the Asia-Pacific region experienced a significant improvement in gross margin, a full 2.0 percentage points year-over-year. This was largely driven by the successful launch of our new mid-range smartphones, which resonated particularly well in emerging markets within the region. Furthermore, we’re seeing increasing adoption of our cloud services across Asia-Pacific, and these services carry a higher margin than our traditional hardware sales. We also benefited from effective cost management and supply chain optimization within the region.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of operating margin and the strategic actions you're taking to address the challenges you faced in Q2?

Marcus Lee:
Sure. While our Q2 operating margin fell slightly short of our initial guidance, we’re taking decisive action to improve our performance in the second half of the year. This includes aggressively managing costs across all business segments, shifting our focus to higher-margin products and services, strengthening our partnerships, and optimizing our marketing spend. We are also closely monitoring macroeconomic factors and making adjustments to our strategy as needed to ensure we deliver sustainable value to our shareholders. We expect to see the benefits of these actions materialize in the coming quarters.

Analyst 3:
With regard to revenue versus guidance, how does the company plan to address the weaker-than-expected performance in the Display Panel division?

David Chen:
We are actively addressing the challenges in the Display Panel division through diversification. We're expanding our product portfolio to include more value-added products, such as OLED panels for automotive and AR/VR applications. We’re also implementing measures to diversify our supply chain and secure critical components to mitigate the impact of disruptions, and focusing on cost reduction initiatives to improve profitability and offset the impact of pricing pressure. Finally, we are shifting our focus towards premium products in the CE division to maintain margins and cater to high-end consumers.

aspect_summary.P&L (revenue and gross margin) guidance: For Q3 2020, revenue is projected to be between $1.95 billion and $2.05 billion, an 8% to 12% decrease sequentially, but a 10% to 15% increase year-over-year. Gross margin is expected to be between 38% and 40%, a decrease of 200 to 400 basis points from Q2 2020.
aspect_summary.sales guidance, forecast, or trend by se: In Q3 2024, Enterprise Storage bit shipments are expected to decrease by 3% sequentially, but revenue is projected to increase by 15% year-over-year to $2.3 billion. Client SSD bit shipments are expected to be flat sequentially, with revenue decreasing 6% year-over-year to $1.1 billion. Mobile segment bit shipments are expected to increase by 2% sequentially, with revenue increasing 4% year-over-year to $800 million. The Consumer segment is expected to see a 5% sequential decrease in bit shipments and a 10% decrease in revenue year-over-year to $300 million. Full year 2024 bit growth is projected to be in the low single digits, slightly below the overall market growth, but revenue growth is expected to be higher than bit growth.
aspect_summary.Operating margin results, QoQ changes, Y: Q2 2024 operating margin was 18.2%, down from 20.1% in Q1 2024 and below the guidance of 19.0% to 20.0%. The QoQ decrease was due to seasonal weakness in consumer electronics, increased competition in LCD panels, and increased marketing spend. Compared to Q2 2023, the operating margin improved from 17.5% to 18.2% due to improvements in the mobile business product mix and cost optimization efforts. The shortfall from guidance was due to a stronger-than-expected consumer electronics slowdown, increased competition in LCD panels, and geopolitical factors.
aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Q1 2024 total consolidated revenue reached KRW 55.3 trillion, representing a 7.6% decrease compared to Q4 2023 (KRW 59.8 trillion). However, on a year-over-year basis, revenue saw a positive growth of 5.6% compared to Q1 2023 (KRW 52.4 trillion). The sequential decline reflects the anticipated seasonal weakness in Display Panel and Consumer Electronics divisions, exacerbated by persistent disruptions related to the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing global supply chain constraints. The YoY growth was primarily driven by strong demand in the memory semiconductor market and increased component sales linked to robust mobile device production from key customers. Q1 2024 revenue fell short of guidance (KRW 57 trillion) by approximately 3% due to weaker-than-expected display panel performance, persistent supply chain disruptions, and conservative guidance for memory.
aspect_summary.Gross margin results, QoQ changes, YoY c: Q3 2024 gross profit was KRW20.5 trillion, a decrease of KRW0.8 trillion compared to Q2 2024. Gross margin improved slightly to 37.1%, exceeding the guidance of 36.5%. The QoQ increase was primarily attributable to the ongoing "Project Phoenix" initiative, focused on streamlining supply chain operations and negotiating more favorable component pricing. Year-over-year, gross profit increased by KRW1.2 trillion, and the gross margin improved from 35.5% to 37.1%, a 1.6 percentage point improvement. The actual gross margin exceeded guidance by 0.6 percentage points due to stronger-than-anticipated enterprise sales, favorable currency exchange rates, and the delayed impact of component price increases.
